npl_ratio.definition: Tỷ lệ nợ xấu: ratio of non-performing loans (Groups 3-5 per TT11) to total outstanding loans

car.definition: Capital Adequacy Ratio (Tỷ lệ an toàn vốn): total regulatory capital divided by risk-weighted assets. Minimum 8% per SBV Basel III adoption

lcr.definition: Liquidity Coverage Ratio (Tỷ lệ bao phủ thanh khoản): high-quality liquid assets divided by total net cash outflows over 30 days

nim.definition: Net Interest Margin (Tỷ lệ thu nhập lãi thuần): net interest income divided by average earning assets

cir.definition: Cost-to-Income Ratio (Tỷ lệ chi phí/thu nhập): operating expenses divided by operating income

cic_credit_score.definition: Vietnam National Credit Information Center score ranging 300-900, used for credit assessment
cic_credit_score.factors: Payment history (35%), Credit utilization (30%), Credit history length (15%), Credit mix (10%), New credit (10%)

str_threshold.definition: Cash transaction threshold for CTR reporting: VND 400,000,000 (~USD 16,000). Electronic transfer threshold: VND 500,000,000 (~USD 20,000)

single_customer_exposure.definition: Maximum lending exposure to a single customer: 15% of bank's equity capital

rag_chunks: NPL (Non-Performing Loan) classification in Vietnam follows SBV Circular 11/2021: Group 1 (current, ≤10 days overdue, 0% provision), Group 2 (special mention, 11-90 days, 5%), Group 3 (substandard, 91-180 days, 20%), Group 4 (doubtful, 181-360 days, 50%), Group 5 (loss, >360 days, 100%). Banks must classify and provision monthly. NPL ratio target is <3%.

Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) in Vietnam per SBV Circular 22/2019: minimum 8% = (Tier 1 + Tier 2 Capital) / Risk-Weighted Assets. Other key ratios: short-term capital for medium/long-term lending ≤30%, single customer exposure ≤15% of equity, related party exposure ≤5% of equity, LCR ≥100%.

Vietnamese AML/CFT framework per Nghị định 116/2013 and Luật PCRT 2022: Cash transaction reporting threshold VND 400 million. Electronic transfer threshold VND 500 million. STR must be filed within 48 hours of suspicious activity confirmation. CDD required for all new customers; EDD for PEPs and high-risk customers.

Credit process in Vietnamese banking follows TT39/2016: RM submits application → CIC credit bureau check → Credit analysis (DTI, LTV, cash flow) → Collateral valuation → Approval authority based on amount (officer <500M, manager 500M-2B, branch director 2B-10B, division head 10B-50B, C-suite 50B-200B, credit committee >200B VND) → Legal documentation → Disbursement.

eKYC in Vietnam per TT16/2020: requires CCCD chip reading (NFC), facial recognition matching (>95% confidence), liveness detection, OTP verification. Three account tiers: Tier 1 (basic, limited transactions), Tier 2 (standard, video eKYC), Tier 3 (full, advanced eKYC or branch visit). Digital banking features include VietQR payments, Napas 24/7 transfers, mobile banking.

Vietnamese banking compliance officer (Giám đốc Tuân thủ) manages: SBV inspection preparation, AML/CFT program, three lines of defense (TT13/2018), regulatory change tracking, staff training. Key circulars: TT13 (internal controls), TT22 (prudential ratios), TT39 (lending), TT16 (e-banking), NĐ116 (AML/CFT).

CIC (Vietnam National Credit Information Center) provides credit scores ranging 300-900. Factors: payment history (35%), credit utilization (30%), credit history length (15%), credit mix (10%), new credit (10%). Banks must query CIC before lending. Group 5 classification disqualifies new credit.

Vietnamese banking handoff chain: eKYC → Account Opening (5 min SLA). Loan Application → CIC Check → Credit Analysis → Legal → Disbursement. AML Alert → Investigation (24h) → STR Filing (48h to AMLD). NPL trigger → Classification (5 days) → Recovery Plan (15 days). Trade Finance: L/C → Document Check (UCP 600) → FX Limit → SWIFT Release.
rag_chunks_v6: The Chief Compliance Officer (Giám đốc Tuân thủ) of a Vietnamese bank is the regulatory navigator and AML/CFT gatekeeper. KPIs: zero critical findings from SBV inspections, STRs filed within 3 working days of detection, more than 95% of staff completing AML/CFT training, 100% of SBV circulars mapped to internal policies, and under 24 hours to respond to a critical compliance incident. Reporting duties: STRs to the AMLD, CTRs for cash over VND 400 million, monthly SBV reports and quarterly CAR reports.

AML red flags a Vietnamese bank's compliance officer screens for: structuring to stay under the VND 400 million cash threshold, rapid movement of funds, shell-company indicators, inconsistent source of funds, transfers to high-risk jurisdictions and PEP-related transactions. AML/CFT screening weighs transaction amount, customer profile, destination country, transaction frequency and documentation quality, and produces a risk assessment, an STR recommendation, an account action and an enhanced monitoring level. The case escalates to the CEO.

AML escalation in a Vietnamese bank: the AML Analyst raises the alert, the AML Officer investigates, the Chief Compliance Officer files the STR, and freezing an account requires CEO approval. A monitoring alert fires for cash of VND 400 million or more or a suspicious pattern; it carries transaction details, customer profile, alert typology and historical patterns, must be reviewed within 24 hours, and the STR is filed within 3 working days of detection. Records are kept for 5 years and customers are screened against sanctions lists.

The Chief Risk Officer (Giám đốc Quản lý Rủi ro) is the bank's enterprise risk guardian and Basel III architect. KPIs: NPL ratio under 3% per Circular 31, provision coverage of bad debt above 100%, VaR within approved limits, internal rating model Gini coefficient above 0.40, and quarterly ICAAP stress testing. Credit risk assessment weighs PD, LGD, EAD, collateral coverage, industry risk rating and concentration risk, and outputs an internal risk rating, a credit limit recommendation, risk-premium pricing and a monitoring frequency, escalating to the Board Risk Committee.

Debt classification under Circular 31/2024 weighs days past due, restructuring history, collateral value and the borrower's financial condition, and outputs the debt group (1 to 5), the specific provision amount and a recovery action plan. When a loan is classified Group 3 or worse, Risk Management hands it to Recovery & Legal with the loan details, classification group, collateral status and borrower condition: classification within 5 days of the trigger and a recovery plan within 15 days.

The CFO (Giám đốc Tài chính) of a Vietnamese bank chairs ALCO. KPIs: CAR of at least 8% per Circular 41, LCR and NSFR of at least 100% as internal Basel III targets, NIM, cost-to-income ratio under 50% and ROE above 15%. Capital allocation weighs budget availability, expected ROA, payback period, CAR impact and strategic alignment, escalating to the CEO. Liquidity management weighs LCR, NSFR, the cash outflow forecast and interbank market conditions, and decides on interbank borrowing, an SBV refinancing request or an asset liquidation plan.

Key bank ratios: NIM (Tỷ lệ thu nhập lãi thuần) is net interest income over average earning assets, healthy at 3-5%. CIR (Tỷ lệ chi phí/thu nhập) is operating expenses over operating income, healthy below 50% and world class below 40%. LCR is high-quality liquid assets over total net cash outflows across 30 days, a Basel III measure with a 100% benchmark (not an SBV legal minimum), healthy above 120%. CAR is healthy at 10% or more against the 8% minimum. An NPL ratio below 1.5% is world class.

Credit handoff in a Vietnamese bank under Circular 39/2016: the Relationship Manager sends the Credit Officer the applicant's CCCD, income documents, CIC report, collateral details and loan purpose. Review starts within 24 hours; retail decisions take 3-5 days and corporate decisions 10-20 days. Once credit is approved, the Credit Officer passes the approved facilities, terms, collateral requirements and authorised signatories to Legal, which prepares documentation within 5 business days. Circular 39 requires credit assessment before approval, collateral documentation, loan purpose verification, disbursement control and post-disbursement monitoring.

Credit approval authority in a Vietnamese bank: L1 officer below VND 500 million, L2 manager VND 500 million to 2 billion, L3 branch director VND 2 to 10 billion, L4 division head VND 10 to 50 billion, L5 C-suite VND 50 to 200 billion, L6 credit committee above VND 200 billion, and L7 the board for exposure above 13% of equity, the 2026 single-customer limit under Law 32/2024. Exposure to related parties is capped at 5% of equity.

Payment accounts and eKYC under Circular 17/2024 and Decision 2345/QĐ-NHNN require eKYC with the chip-based ID card, biometric verification against the chip ID, biometric authentication above VND 10 million per transfer or VND 20 million a day, eKYC account limits and device binding. After eKYC succeeds (chip, facial match and liveness), the Digital Onboarding Agent hands the Account Operations Agent the CCCD number, facial match score, liveness result, NFC chip data and AML screening result, and the account is created within 5 minutes.

The Branch Manager (Giám đốc Chi nhánh) is the local operations leader. KPIs: deposit growth (tăng trưởng huy động) and loan growth (tăng trưởng tín dụng) year on year, branch NPL ratio below 2%, NPS above 70 and the cross-sell ratio. Branch vocabulary: huy động (deposit mobilisation), tín dụng (credit), KHCN (retail customers), KHDN (corporate customers), sổ đỏ (land-use certificate used as collateral), thẩm định (appraisal) and giải ngân (disbursement).
